techniques.technique_steps:
1. Butterfly guard, bottom: close the distance with a strong posture, elbows closed but able to maneuver, and attack so the opponent has to defend.
2. Take a good underhook: send the hand deeper, higher and farther, and keep the elbow up rather than clamping it down.
3. Push his elbow in and concentrate on keeping that arm in; do not push the elbow back and do not pull it in.
4. Once the underhook is clamped and the elbow is in, go immediately with the sweep; do not hold that position.
5. Close the distance with the hook, bringing the butt as close as possible to the heels.
6. Scoop and pull his weight off the ground, then guide that weight so his back goes to the floor, not onto you.
7. Lift as high as needed while turning halfway so your shoulder and side go to the floor, not a flat back.
8. Keep the lifting knee pointed up and out, never in, until he falls, so the knee does not buckle and collapse the sweep.
9. Post the other knee close, down, and closed to help get him off the ground, then lift that hook as well.
10. Come up and hold the top position, even if the landing is half guard.
techniques.main_ideas: Attack so he has to defend; a deep no-gi underhook with the elbow up only works if you push his elbow in and go immediately. Scoop him off the ground and turn onto your shoulder so his back hits the mat, not you. Keep the lifting knee pointed out until he falls, and hold top even if you land in half guard.
